newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends firmer on higher stocks, bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends firmer on higher stocks, bonds.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended firmer on Monday at C$1.3865 (US$0.7212) from Friday's close of C$1.3915 (US$0.7186), powered by stronger stocks and bonds, dealers said.
* They said a 24-point rally on the Toronto Stock Exchange and 75-cent rally in the long end of the Canadian bond market created enough buying interest to drive up the currency.
The Canadian dollar ended firmer on Monday at C$1.3865 (US$0.7212) from Friday's close of C$1.3915 (US$0.7186), powered by stronger stocks and bonds.

Dealers said a 24-point rally on the Toronto Stock Exchange and 75-cent rally in the long end of the Canadian bond market created enough buying interest to drive up the currency when most were expecting it to weaken.

"I guess we all started off the day saying C$1.40 (US$0.7142) was in the cards this week and clearly it's done a bit better than anticipated," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange at CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc.

Traders said the currency broke through the crucial C$1.3880 (US$0.7204) level, but its strength is not expected to last because of speculation about widening interest rate spreads between Canada and the U.S.
"We'll have to see if we see any selling against the yen overnight because last night they sold Canada against the yen, which pushed it up to C$1.3944 (US$0.7171)," Wateridge said.

On March 25, the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked interest rates by 25 basis points, widening the spread between U.S. and Canadian short-term rates. Since then pressure on the Bank of Canada to raise rates has depressed the Canadian dollar.

Economists said the Bank of Canada was caught in a Catch-22 situation, where money market investors were selling Canadian dollar short-term debt instruments for U.S. ones to get gains on yields of up to 250 basis points.
But Canada's economy has made a fragile recovery based on lower interest rates and there is little sign of a domestic economic need for the Bank of Canada to raise rates.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar jumped to 1.2340 marks from Friday's close of 1.2111 marks and soared to 90.60 from Friday's 89.24 yen.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
